hunks.baseline: They called it an office, but it was a building. This six-story building sat on prime real estate right by the station, and hundreds of Hunters came through it every day.
hunks.sol: They called it an office, but it occupied an entire six-story building on prime real estate right by the station. Hundreds of Hunters passed through its doors every day.

hunks.baseline: After working through the long line, I reached the counter. The woman there asked in a businesslike tone,
hunks.sol: After waiting through the long line, I reached the counter. The woman behind it asked in a businesslike tone,

hunks.baseline: Back when I was a rookie, I’d graduated from the Hunter Training Center with excellent scores. But almost nowhere needed an F-rank Hunter like me, and the contracts a few small and midsize Guilds offered like they were doing me a favor were highway robbery.
hunks.sol: Back when I was a rookie, I’d graduated from the Hunter Training Center with excellent scores. But hardly anyone needed an F-rank Hunter like me, and the contracts a few small and midsize Guilds offered as if they were doing me a favor were highway robbery.

hunks.baseline: So I’d found this place. The region had been different, though.
hunks.sol: So I’d come here instead. To a different branch, though.

hunks.baseline: This six-story building was a pyramid all by itself. The first floor took E- and F-ranks. You needed at least D-rank to set foot on the second.
hunks.sol: This six-story building was a pyramid unto itself. The first floor took E- and F-ranks. You needed to be at least D-rank to set foot on the second.

hunks.baseline: Some people got angry, asking if this wasn’t just open discrimination.
hunks.sol: Some people got angry and asked if that wasn’t blatant discrimination.

hunks.baseline: I’d lasted seven years in this business and taken every kind of dirty treatment there was. I’d long since passed the point of being picky.
hunks.sol: I’d lasted seven years in this business and seen every ugly side of it. I’d long since passed the point where I could afford to be picky.

hunks.baseline: I started walking with that thought when—
hunks.sol: I had just started walking when—

hunks.baseline: I turned at the gravelly voice. Some hairy guy was grinning at me.
hunks.sol: I turned toward the gravelly voice. Some hairy guy was grinning at me.

hunks.baseline: He just looked so much like a bandit that everyone called him Im Kkeokjeong[^1].
hunks.sol: He looked so much like a bandit that everyone called him Im Kkeokjeong.[^1]

hunks.baseline: “Life as an F-rank Hunter is always the same. How about you?”
hunks.sol: “Life as an F-rank Hunter is pretty much the same for all of us. How about you?”

hunks.baseline: How many years apart were we again? It was hazy.
hunks.sol: How many years apart were we again? I couldn’t quite remember.

hunks.baseline: But the people skills I’d honed over the years paid off. I somehow managed to force a smile.
hunks.sol: But the social skills I’d honed over the years came through for me. I somehow managed to force a smile.

hunks.baseline: “Right. I’ll just call you hyung.”
hunks.sol: “You’re right. I’ll just call you hyung.”

hunks.baseline: His hearty laugh rolled through the hall. Nearly a hundred people looked over, then looked away.
hunks.sol: His hearty laughter rang through the hall. Nearly a hundred people looked over, then turned away.

hunks.baseline: In a way, it was a shallow connection. We’d run into each other every day for about half a year at the Ilsan office, and sometimes worked together. That was about it.
hunks.sol: Ours wasn’t exactly a deep connection. We’d seen each other almost every day for about half a year at the Ilsan office and worked together a few times. That was about it.

hunks.baseline: Sometimes having him next to me was embarrassing.
hunks.sol: Sometimes it was embarrassing to be around him.

hunks.baseline: “The yulmu tea here is incredible. And the chairs in the hall are nice and soft.”
hunks.sol: “The yulmu tea here is incredible. The chairs in the hall are nice and soft too.”

hunks.baseline: Im Kkeokjeong knocked back a mouthful of yulmu tea[^2] and tipped his chair as far as it would go.
hunks.sol: Im Kkeokjeong tossed back his yulmu tea[^2] in one gulp and leaned his chair as far back as it would go.

hunks.baseline: From the way he did it, this clearly wasn’t his first or second visit.
hunks.sol: Judging by how comfortable he looked, this clearly wasn’t his first or second visit.

hunks.baseline: “Not every day. I drop by now and then. Once I got married and had kids, I started watching myself. Heh heh.”
hunks.sol: “Not every day. I drop by now and then. Once I got married and had kids, I started being more careful. Heh heh.”

hunks.baseline: It seemed he’d started a family while we were out of touch. When I congratulated him, Im Kkeokjeong scratched his head.
hunks.sol: Apparently, he’d started a family while we were out of touch. When I congratulated him, Im Kkeokjeong scratched his head.

hunks.baseline: “What’s so great about that.”
hunks.sol: “What’s so special about that?”

hunks.baseline: He was being modest, but a big deal was a big deal. He’d worked as a Hunter—an F-rank Hunter—for more than twenty years and still managed to build a family.
hunks.sol: He was being modest, but it was a big deal. He’d spent more than twenty years working as a Hunter—an F-rank Hunter—and still managed to build a family.

hunks.baseline: I wondered if the Im Kkeokjeong in front of me might be my future self.
hunks.sol: I wondered if the Im Kkeokjeong before me might be a glimpse of my own future.

hunks.baseline: *Assuming I lived to that age first.*
hunks.sol: *Assuming I live to that age.*

hunks.baseline: Being a Hunter wasn’t a career you could keep up for long. Plenty of people retired the moment they finished the ten years that qualified them for a pension.
hunks.sol: Being a Hunter wasn’t a career you could keep up for long. Plenty of people retired the moment they completed the ten years needed to qualify for a pension.

hunks.baseline: “Anyway, you’re starting to look the part. When I first saw you, you were completely frozen. Could barely even talk.”
hunks.sol: “Anyway, you’re starting to look the part. When I first met you, you were so nervous you could barely talk.”

hunks.baseline: “Of course. I’ve got seven years in.”
hunks.sol: “Of course. I’ve got seven years under my belt now.”

hunks.baseline: “So you’ve just been bouncing around offices ever since? Didn’t you sign with a small or midsize Guild on fairly decent terms? So, So… what was the name again?”
hunks.sol: “So you’ve been bouncing around manpower offices ever since? Didn’t you sign a fairly decent contract with some small or midsize Guild? So, So… what was it called again?”

hunks.baseline: “Hahaha! Good for you. The Guild’s name was lousy, too. What the hell is Sopung? It’s not like you’re going on a picnic to a Gate.”
hunks.sol: “Hahaha! Good for you. The Guild’s name was lousy anyway. Sopung? What kind of name is that? It’s not like you’re going on a picnic to a Gate.”

hunks.baseline: “No, not that sopung. It’s a place name. They’re near Bucheon Sopung Terminal, so Sopung Guild.”
hunks.sol: “No, not that kind of sopung. It’s a place name. They’re near Bucheon Sopung Terminal, so they’re called Sopung Guild.”

hunks.baseline: The conversation that followed was pretty useful. Im Kkeokjeong was a regular at the manpower office, after all, and a veteran Hunter with decent information and his own hard-earned know-how.
hunks.sol: The conversation that followed was surprisingly useful. Im Kkeokjeong was a regular at the manpower office, after all, and a veteran Hunter with good information and plenty of hard-earned tricks of the trade.

hunks.baseline: “The office takes a ten percent commission. That’s standard. But the batting average here is pretty good.”
hunks.sol: “The office takes a ten percent commission. That’s standard. But this branch has a pretty good batting average.”

hunks.baseline: *Batting average* was slang in this business for the odds of getting hired. For someone whose immediate goal was a day’s pay, that was good news.
hunks.sol: *Batting average* was industry slang for your odds of getting hired. For someone whose immediate goal was a day’s pay, that was good news.

hunks.baseline: At last, the first batter was up. And it would only be my turn after all the E-rank Hunters had left.
hunks.sol: At last, the first batter was up. My turn would come only after all the E-rank Hunters had gone.

hunks.baseline: “I’ll go ahead.”
hunks.sol: “I’ll go on ahead.”

hunks.baseline: Im Kkeokjeong—or rather, Im Hyeokjun—slung a large bag of armor and weapons over his shoulder and gave a sheepish laugh.
hunks.sol: Im Kkeokjeong—or rather, Im Hyeokjun—slung a large bag of armor and weapons over his shoulder and chuckled.

hunks.baseline: *No wonder his expression looked off.*
hunks.sol: *No wonder he was acting strange.*

hunks.baseline: The man had clearly worked himself to the bone while I wasn’t looking.
hunks.sol: He must have worked himself to the bone while we were out of touch.

hunks.baseline: It was only one step, but ranking up on an F-rank’s potential was no easy feat.
hunks.sol: It was only a single step up, but advancing beyond F-rank despite an F-rank’s potential was no easy feat.

hunks.baseline: “See you again.”
hunks.sol: “See you around.”

hunks.baseline: “Yes. See you.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah. See you.”

hunks.baseline: Him walking out of the hall was the start. The speakers began pouring out names like they meant it.
hunks.sol: His departure from the hall opened the floodgates. The speakers began rattling off names one after another.

hunks.baseline: E-rank this person, E-rank that person, E-rank…
hunks.sol: E-rank so-and-so, E-rank somebody else, E-rank…

hunks.baseline: A man in a white linen shirt was waiting in the lobby. Without preamble, he held out a contract with a blank face.
hunks.sol: A man in a white linen shirt was waiting in the lobby. Without so much as a greeting, he held out a contract, his expression flat.

hunks.baseline: *This guy’s way of talking is seriously irritating.*
hunks.sol: *This guy’s tone is seriously irritating.*

hunks.baseline: I glared from the contract to the man’s face and back.
hunks.sol: I looked from the contract to the man’s face and back again.

hunks.baseline: “After the raid, we divide the proceeds fairly by contribution. Then we take twenty percent of the amount you receive.”
hunks.sol: “After the raid, the proceeds will be distributed fairly according to contribution. We’ll take twenty percent of your share.”

hunks.baseline: *Did this guy’s tongue get cut in half?*
hunks.sol: *Did this guy lose half his tongue?*

hunks.baseline: “Gate rank.”
hunks.sol: “Gate rank?”

hunks.baseline: “Rejected.”
hunks.sol: “Pass.”

hunks.baseline: “The positions are full. You’ll be a porter.”
hunks.sol: “The combat positions are full. You’ll be a porter.”

hunks.baseline: “Por-ter?”
hunks.sol: “A por-ter?”

hunks.baseline: The shirt guy glared at me, looking down his nose.
hunks.sol: The man in the linen shirt glared down his nose at me.

hunks.baseline: I’d flinched at E-rank Gate, but I was only going as a porter, so it didn’t matter. Skin a few monsters, haul a pack for a while, and part ways in a good mood.
hunks.sol: I’d flinched when I heard it was an E-rank Gate, but I was only going as a porter, so it didn’t matter. I’d skin a few monsters, haul a pack around, then part ways with everyone in a good mood.

hunks.baseline: “All signed.”
hunks.sol: “All done.”

hunks.baseline: “So where are we going now? We taking a van?”
hunks.sol: “So where are we going? Are we taking a van?”

hunks.baseline: “There’s a van waiting outside.”
hunks.sol: “There’s one waiting outside.”

hunks.baseline: “Oh, that one? Looks nice. Bet the AC’s blasting too.”
hunks.sol: “Oh, that one? Looks nice. Bet the AC works great too.”

hunks.baseline: “Guess I was last? There are already a few people here… Huh? Kkeokjeong hyung!”
hunks.sol: “Guess I was the last one. There are already a few people here… Huh? Kkeokjeong hyung!”

hunks.baseline: Im Kkeokjeong was waiting to load his bags into the bus’s trunk. He grinned wide.
hunks.sol: Im Kkeokjeong was waiting to load his bag into the vehicle’s luggage compartment. His face lit up.

hunks.baseline: “You’re coming too. Great!”
hunks.sol: “You’re coming too. That’s great!”

hunks.baseline: “Right? I must really have a connection with you, hyung.”
hunks.sol: “Looks like you and I really do have a connection, hyung.”

hunks.baseline: Maybe it was the heat, but the shirt guy’s face looked years older.
hunks.sol: Maybe it was the heat, but the man in the linen shirt suddenly looked years older.

hunks.baseline: The bus pulled out. From the passenger seat, the shirt guy said we’d arrive within twenty minutes, then closed his eyes.
hunks.sol: The minibus pulled away. From the passenger seat, the man in the linen shirt said we’d arrive within twenty minutes, then closed his eyes.

hunks.baseline: “All right, everyone, say hello. This is a younger brother I know.”
hunks.sol: “All right, everyone, say hello. This is a younger friend of mine.”

hunks.baseline: Now that I looked, they all knew each other. I dipped my head.
hunks.sol: Now that I looked, they all seemed to know one another. I bowed my head.

hunks.baseline: “Tall young fellow. Looks like he can fight.”
hunks.sol: “Tall, handsome young fellow. Looks like he can fight.”

hunks.baseline: There were three new people in all, men in their late thirties or early forties. In that warm atmosphere, Im Kkeokjeong explained.
hunks.sol: There were three new faces, all men in their late thirties or early forties. As the warm introductions continued, Im Kkeokjeong explained.

hunks.baseline: “These guys are all E-rank. I’ve known them a long time. Over ten years now.”
hunks.sol: “These guys are all E-rank. I’ve known them for a long time. More than ten years now.”

hunks.baseline: Meaning they all had at least ten years in. I had enough experience that nobody was going to call me a rookie wherever I went, but these guys were on another level entirely.
hunks.sol: That meant every one of them had at least ten years of experience. I’d been around long enough that nobody would call me a rookie, but these guys were on another level.

hunks.baseline: *Old-timer party.*
hunks.sol: *A whole party of old-timers.*

hunks.baseline: People like them pulled their weight wherever they went. In a pinch, they were much better than a middling D-rank.
hunks.sol: People like them pulled their weight wherever they went. In an emergency, they were far more dependable than some half-baked D-rank.

hunks.baseline: “So what’s the young guy’s rank?”
hunks.sol: “So what rank are you, young man?”

hunks.baseline: “Ah. That so? How many years?”
hunks.sol: “Ah. That so? How long have you been at it?”

hunks.baseline: “Seven.”
hunks.sol: “Seven years.”

hunks.baseline: The mood went lukewarm. If my first raid started like this, that would be a problem.
hunks.sol: The response was lukewarm. This wasn’t how I wanted my first raid back to start.

hunks.baseline: I ran my mouth before it could settle.
hunks.sol: I hurried to explain.

hunks.baseline: “I won’t be in combat at all. I’m joining as a porter, so you don’t have to worry…”
hunks.sol: “I won’t be taking part in combat. I’m joining as a porter, so you don’t need to worry…”

hunks.baseline: The three men stared at me blankly.
hunks.sol: The three men stared blankly at me.

hunks.baseline: “Why the extra explanation? We gonna eat you?”
hunks.sol: “Why the long explanation? You think we’re going to eat you?”

hunks.baseline: “Drop it. If he’s been knocking around for seven years, he knows enough.”
hunks.sol: “Drop it. If he’s been knocking around for seven years, he knows what he’s doing.”

hunks.baseline: “If Kkeokjeong hyung recommended him, that’s enough. Team Leader Choi must’ve thought he was all right too, or he wouldn’t have said yes.”
hunks.sol: “If Kkeokjeong hyung recommended him, that’s good enough. Team Leader Choi must’ve thought he was all right too, or he wouldn’t have agreed.”

hunks.baseline: I didn’t know the exact details, but I could more or less see how this had gone.
hunks.sol: I didn’t know the exact details, but I could more or less piece together what had happened.

hunks.baseline: Im Kkeokjeong had recommended me. To the shirt guy—Team Leader Choi.
hunks.sol: Im Kkeokjeong had recommended me to the man in the linen shirt—Team Leader Choi.

hunks.baseline: Im Kkeokjeong waved his hands, his face bright red.
hunks.sol: Im Kkeokjeong waved his hands, his face turning bright red.

hunks.baseline: “It’s written all over him. How did that hyung ever get married?”
hunks.sol: “It’s written all over your face. How did this hyung ever manage to get married?”

hunks.baseline: “Good deeds are supposed to come to light. Why live hiding them?”
hunks.sol: “Good deeds are supposed to come to light. Why hide them?”

hunks.baseline: “Right. You think so too, don’t you?”
hunks.sol: “Exactly. You think so too, don’t you?”

hunks.baseline: I’d thought of Im Kkeokjeong as one of the many people I’d crossed paths with for a moment and moved on from. Meeting him again, he was more simple and warmhearted than I’d expected.
hunks.sol: I’d thought of Im Kkeokjeong as one of the countless people I’d briefly crossed paths with and then moved on from. Meeting him again, I realized he was far more guileless and warmhearted than I’d expected.

hunks.baseline: The way they kept saying Team Leader Choi, Team Leader Choi, I figured their friendship had played a part in my contract too.
hunks.sol: Judging by the way they kept mentioning Team Leader Choi, I figured their friendship had played a part in my contract too.

hunks.baseline: The man in question answered Im Kkeokjeong’s awkward excuse.
hunks.sol: The man himself answered Im Kkeokjeong’s awkward protest.

hunks.baseline: The shirt guy had opened his eyes at some point. No—Team Leader Choi. He spoke to us.
hunks.sol: The man in the linen shirt had opened his eyes at some point. No—Team Leader Choi. He addressed us.

hunks.baseline: “We’ve arrived.”
hunks.sol: “We’re here.”

hunks.baseline: I looked over. A four-meter-high Gate was drawing closer. At its center, a vortex of mana churned, ready to suck us in.
hunks.sol: I turned my head. A four-meter-high Gate loomed closer. At its center, a vortex of mana churned, ready to suck us in.

hunks.baseline:
[^1]: Famous Joseon-era folk-hero bandit; the nickname comes from his looks.
[^2]: Yulmu tea is a sweet Korean grain drink, commonly served hot or cold.
hunks.sol:
[^1]: Im Kkeokjeong was a famous Joseon-era bandit and folk hero; the nickname comes from the man’s bandit-like appearance.
[^2]: Yulmu tea is a sweet Korean grain drink commonly served hot or cold.
